## Applied Statistics · Machine Learning · Biomedical Data Science

I am an applied statistician and biomedical data science researcher developing reliable, interpretable, and reproducible machine-learning methods for complex biomedical data.

My work focuses on high-dimensional and small-sample prediction, external validation, model calibration, feature-selection stability, and clinically meaningful evaluation.

[Explore my research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [View publications](publications.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [Download CV](assets/Enock_Kumi_Ackaah_CV.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

## Research at a glance

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.focus-card}
### Reliable biomedical AI

Evaluating whether predictive performance remains stable across samples, validation settings, and external populations.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
### High-dimensional data

Developing leakage-safe analyses for RNA-sequencing, DNA-methylation, clinical, and multimodal biomedical datasets.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
### Interpretability and validation

Studying feature stability, calibration, uncertainty, reproducibility, and human oversight in healthcare prediction models.
:::

## Current research

### Statistical Reliability of High-Dimensional Breast Cancer RNA-Sequencing Models

This project examines how development sample size affects predictive performance, feature-selection stability, coefficient-direction reproducibility, probability accuracy, and external generalization in estrogen-receptor status prediction.

[Project details](research.qmd#statistical-reliability-of-high-dimensional-breast-cancer-rna-sequencing-models) · [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Enock-ackaah/statistical-reliability-high-dimensional-er-models) · [Zenodo release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21524693)
